_meta.source: docs/CONTENT.md draft 2, docs/DESIGN.md revision 4, docs/tech/balance.md stat sheet
_meta.status: staging input for the catalogue importer; written by an AI, not yet reviewed by the owner
_meta.keyed_by: The building's English name. Where CONTENT.md lists a set on one line (for example 'Cistern (small, medium, large)') each building has its own entry and 'content_md' gives the CONTENT.md label.

suggested_mod_key_pattern.name: Pandaborn.Building.<Id>.DisplayName
suggested_mod_key_pattern.note: <Id> is the 'id' field without its Pandaborn prefix. Loc keys must begin with Pandaborn (docs/ENGINEERING.md). A mod key equal to a vanilla key replaces the vanilla text for every faction, so a re-themed building that needs different words must point its Inkpaws template at a new key.

field_rules.basis: 'new' = an Inkpaws building with its own name. 'rethemed' = a vanilla building in Inkpaw materials that keeps its vanilla name.
field_rules.name: A string is new text. null means: keep the vanilla key named in 'vanilla_id'.
field_rules.description: A string is new text. null means: keep the vanilla description key. Vanilla text is already translated into every language the game ships, so null is preferred wherever the vanilla words are true and do not mention beavers.
field_rules.flavor: Same rule as description. At most one short line.
field_rules.reuse: Optional. Names a vanilla loc key to point at instead of writing new text, when a new building does exactly what a vanilla one does.
field_rules.why: For re-themed buildings: why the vanilla text was replaced.
field_rules.status_and_tooltip_lines: Live in messages.json. 'see' lists the message ids that belong on this building's panel.

_meta.icons_in_text: [sun] and [moon] stand for the day and night icons. The importer replaces them with the sprite tag the interface uses.
_meta.highlight_tags: <YellowHighlight>…</YellowHighlight> is the vanilla keyword tag and is used the same way here.

Village Hall.name: Village Hall
Village Hall.description: The heart of a district, with its own population, goods and path network. Employs builders.
Village Hall.note: The flavor line is the motto, as on the vanilla District Center. It must match 'motto' in faction.json.

Builders' Hut.flavor: When the bell rings, the hammer goes down. The nail can wait until morning.

Hauling Post.flavor: An Inkpaw hauler carries more on every trip and sees no reason to hurry.
Hauling Post.why: Vanilla flavor mentions beavers and tails.

District Crossing.flavor: Goods cross here every day. News crosses faster.
District Crossing.why: Vanilla flavor is a beaver joke.

Festival Square.name: Festival Square
Festival Square.description: Calls the Lantern Festival and hosts it. Pandas gather here in the evening.
Festival Square.flavor: Swept every morning, just in case.

Den.name: Den
Den.description: A simple home for a small family.
Den.flavor: It smells of bamboo and of whoever napped there last.

Courtyard House.name: Courtyard House
Courtyard House.description: A larger home built around a shared yard.
Courtyard House.flavor: The yard is for airing bedding, drying vegetables and long conversations.

Terrace House.name: Terrace House
Terrace House.description: A large home for many families. Built to be stacked up a hillside.
Terrace House.flavor: The higher the home, the better the view and the longer the walk to dinner.

Moon Loft.name: Moon Loft
Moon Loft.description: A home on stilts over a path. The first one invites a Ringtail family; kits are raised here while there is night work.
Moon Loft.flavor: A lantern in a high window is an old invitation.
Moon Loft.note: Any home takes anyone, so the description never says 'home for Ringtails'.

Gatherer Flag.flavor: A full basket leaves the bushes. A slightly less full basket reaches the warehouse.

Farmstead.description: Employs farmers who plant and harvest shoot bamboo and cabbage on moist ground.
Farmstead.flavor: A field is planted in the morning and admired in the afternoon.
Farmstead.note: CONTENT.md marks it re-themed, but the name is new, so all three strings are new.

Steamer.name: Steamer
Steamer.flavor: Lifting the lid early is the most common kitchen offense in the village.

Pickle Yard.name: Pickle Yard
Pickle Yard.description: Pickles cabbage in clay jars. One cabbage fills several jars, so a small field feeds more villagers.
Pickle Yard.flavor: Every jar belongs to somebody's grandmother, and she knows exactly how many there are.

Paddy House.name: Paddy House
Paddy House.description: Employs paddy farmers who plant and harvest rice, an <YellowHighlight>Aquatic</YellowHighlight> crop that grows in shallow flooded fields.
Paddy House.flavor: Paddy farmers are the only villagers who wear the wide hat, and they do not lend it.
Paddy House.note: 'Aquatic' is the vanilla keyword the game already shows on the plant (NaturalResources.Aquatic).

Tea Roastery.name: Tea Roastery
Tea Roastery.description: Roasts tea leaves. Roasted tea keeps in any warehouse.
Tea Roastery.flavor: The smell reaches the fields well before the bell does.

Trip-Hammer Mill.name: Trip-Hammer Mill
Trip-Hammer Mill.description: Pounds rice into rice flour. Its wheel is driven directly by flowing water: place it on a flume or a stream. Needs no power shafts.
Trip-Hammer Mill.flavor: The water lifts the hammer and lets it fall. The miller mostly watches.

Kitchen.name: Kitchen
Kitchen.description: Cooks sweet rice balls and bamboo seed cakes from rice flour.
Kitchen.flavor: Every cook in the village claims the recipe. All the recipes are the same.

Hot Pot Hall.name: Hot Pot Hall
Hot Pot Hall.description: Cooks hot pot from cabbage, Sichuan pepper and bamboo mushrooms. The best everyday meal in the village.
Hot Pot Hall.flavor: Nobody admits to adding the extra pepper. Everybody reaches for the tea.

Lumberjack Flag.description: Employs a lumberjack who cuts trees for logs and timber bamboo for poles.
Lumberjack Flag.flavor: Lumberjacks cut whatever you mark. They would like it noted that bamboo is lighter.
Lumberjack Flag.why: The Inkpaw lumberjack also cuts timber bamboo, and this is where a player learns that poles need no mill.

Forester.description: Plants timber bamboo, trees and bushes, including tea and Sichuan pepper.
Forester.flavor: Timber bamboo is ready before the forester has finished admiring it.
Forester.why: Names timber bamboo; vanilla flavor mentions beaver society.

Gear Workshop.flavor: A bamboo gear is light, cheap and surprisingly loud.
Gear Workshop.why: Vanilla says 'from planks' and quotes Ol' Kazko.

Paper Mill.description: A mechanized mill that makes paper from poles.
Paper Mill.flavor: Paper goes to lanterns, kites and the Ink Studio, in that order.
Paper Mill.why: Inkpaw paper is made from poles, not logs; vanilla flavor is about beavers eating paper.

Lantern Workshop.name: Lantern Workshop
Lantern Workshop.description: Makes paper lanterns from paper and poles.
Lantern Workshop.flavor: Every lantern is tested once, at dusk, by whoever made it. This is not officially part of the job.

Pole Mill.name: Pole Mill
Pole Mill.flavor: Bamboo grows back in a week. The mill keeps the builders busy until it does.
Pole Mill.note: DESIGN.md 2026-11-14: the vanilla lumber mill (LumberMill.Inkpaws) with its own name; poles are the renamed Plank.

Smoke Kiln.name: Smoke Kiln
Smoke Kiln.description: Cures poles over slow log smoke. Cured poles are the strong material for late construction. Needs no power.
Smoke Kiln.flavor: A pole spends hours in the smoke. The kiln keeper smells of it for days.

Explosives Factory.note: Vanilla text is true and neutral. The vanilla factory already makes fireworks.

Smelter.flavor: The hottest job in the village. Smelters get the first cup of tea, and nobody argues.
Smelter.why: Vanilla flavor mentions the beaver world and burnt fur.

Water Pump.description: Pumps and filters water for the village to drink. Badwater contamination slows down its pumping speed.
Water Pump.why: Vanilla description says 'for beavers to drink'.

Small Cistern.name: Small Cistern
Small Cistern.flavor: The first thing built before a drought and the first thing checked during one.

Medium Cistern.name: Medium Cistern
Medium Cistern.flavor: After its first drought, every village builds one more than it thinks it needs.

Large Cistern.name: Large Cistern
Large Cistern.flavor: When it is full, it is the calmest sight in the village.

Flume.name: Flume
Flume.description: An open bamboo aqueduct. Water runs one way, along the arrow, level or downhill. It never climbs and never leaks.
Flume.flavor: Each length knocks once as the water reaches it. Villagers count the knocks.

Flume Corner.name: Flume Corner
Flume Corner.description: Turns a flume to the left or to the right. Flumes do not bend on their own.
Flume Corner.flavor: Water does not like to turn. It was not asked.

Flume Drop.name: Flume Drop
Flume Drop.description: Steps a flume down one level. Water falls here and cannot come back up.
Flume Drop.flavor: The one part of a flume that cubs are told not to sit under. They sit under it.

Flume Bridge.name: Flume Bridge
Flume Bridge.description: Carries a flume above the ground on bamboo trestles, across dips and gaps.
Flume Bridge.flavor: Everyone who passes looks up at it. It has never dripped.

Flume Gate.name: Flume Gate
Flume Gate.description: The intake of a flume. Sets how much water enters, and shuts itself when the water turns bad.
Flume Gate.flavor: It tastes the water so that the rice does not have to.

Scoop Wheel.name: Scoop Wheel
Scoop Wheel.description: Sits in a current and lifts water one level into a flume. Needs flowing water and no workers. It stops when the current stops.
Scoop Wheel.flavor: The river does the work. In a drought, the river takes time off too.

Paddy Spout.name: Paddy Spout
Paddy Spout.description: Keeps the field in front of it flooded to a shallow set depth. Needs water at its back and walls around the field.
Paddy Spout.flavor: Rice likes to stand in water. The spout decides how much.

Cistern Tap.name: Cistern Tap
Cistern Tap.description: Pours stored water into a flume or a basin, slowly and with no workers of its own. Keeps one strip of ground alive through a drought.
Cistern Tap.flavor: A trickle is not much, until it is the only water moving in the valley.
Cistern Tap.note: CONTENT.md marks it re-themed (vanilla Discharge), but it has a new name, so its strings are new.

Dew Collector.name: Dew Collector
Dew Collector.description: Collects a little drinking water each dawn, and less in a drought. Collectors built close together share the same dew.
Dew Collector.flavor: Not enough to live on. Enough for the first pot of tea.

Treadwheel Lift.name: Treadwheel Lift
Treadwheel Lift.description: Lifts water one level where there is no current. Turned by a worker, so it runs only during the working day.
Treadwheel Lift.flavor: A morning of walking, and nobody has gone anywhere. The water has gone up.

Large Water Pump.description: Pumps and filters large amounts of water for the village to drink. Badwater contamination slows down its pumping speed.
Large Water Pump.flavor: More water than the village can drink in a day. The rest is called a reserve.
Large Water Pump.why: Vanilla description says 'for beavers'; flavor quotes a beaver song.

Mechanical Pump.content_md: Large Water Pump, Mechanical Pumps, Aquifer Drill

Compact Mechanical Pump.content_md: Large Water Pump, Mechanical Pumps, Aquifer Drill

Aquifer Drill.flavor: It leads water up instead of down. The principle is the same. The noise is not.

Badwater Pump.flavor: Pump workers eat their lunch upwind.
Badwater Pump.why: Vanilla flavor is a quote from Suli, a beaver.

Discharge.content_md: Badwater Pump, Discharge, Centrifuge, Dome, Rig
Discharge.flavor: Whatever the village does not want is poured out here, a long way from the tea.
Discharge.why: Vanilla flavor is a quote from Ol' Kazko, a beaver.

Centrifuge.flavor: It spins badwater until the useful part gives up and separates.
Centrifuge.why: Vanilla flavor mentions a Folktails carousel.

Levee.flavor: A flume tells water where to go. A levee tells it where to stop.
Levee.why: Vanilla flavor mentions beaver water engineers.

Floodgate.flavor: Somebody has to decide how high. This takes longer than building it.

Impermeable Floor.flavor: Laid under a pool so that the water stays in the pool.

Dynamite.note: Double Dynamite and Triple Dynamite also keep all vanilla text.

Dry-Stone Wall.name: Dry-Stone Wall
Dry-Stone Wall.description: Stops moisture from spreading through the ground past it.
Dry-Stone Wall.flavor: No mortar and no hurry. Each stone was turned over twice before it was placed.

Bamboo Water Wheel.name: Bamboo Water Wheel
Bamboo Water Wheel.flavor: It turns for as long as the river does, and it does not stop for the bell.

Power Wheel.description: A backup source of power, turned by a worker.
Power Wheel.flavor: It turns only while somebody walks in it. At the bell, it stops with everybody else.
Power Wheel.why: Vanilla says 'beaver-operated'; flavor compares beavers to other rodents.

Kite Windmill.name: Kite Windmill
Kite Windmill.flavor: On a windless day the kites hang still, and everyone pretends not to look up.

Large Kite Windmill.name: Large Kite Windmill
Large Kite Windmill.flavor: More kites, more string, more power. Nobody has volunteered to untangle it.

Power Shaft.note: Vertical Power Shaft also keeps all vanilla text.

Impermeable Power Shaft.flavor: Power passes through. Water does not.
Impermeable Power Shaft.why: Vanilla flavor is a quote from Pina, a beaver.

Inventor.flavor: Inkpaw inventors do their best thinking lying down, and have the notes to prove it.
Inventor.why: Vanilla flavor names Ol' Kazko and beaver inventors.

Star Tower.name: Star Tower
Star Tower.description: Ringtail stargazers study the night sky here and turn what they see into Science Points. Works from the afternoon bell to dawn and needs no power.
Star Tower.flavor: Every star has a name. The Ringtails are still deciding on some of them.

Ox Workshop.name: Ox Workshop
Ox Workshop.description: Builds Wooden Oxen: tireless, strong and slow workers that need no food, no water and no rest.
Ox Workshop.flavor: The first Wooden Ox was built to carry rice. It is still carrying rice.
Ox Workshop.note: CONTENT.md marks it re-themed (vanilla Bot Assembler), but it has a new name. The bot's name is in faction.json.

Small Warehouse.content_md: Warehouses, piles and the underground pile
Small Warehouse.flavor: Everything has a shelf. Finding the shelf is a separate skill.
Small Warehouse.why: Vanilla flavor is a quote from Ma' Ngonel, a beaver.

Medium Warehouse.content_md: Warehouses, piles and the underground pile

Large Warehouse.content_md: Warehouses, piles and the underground pile
Large Warehouse.flavor: Somewhere at the back there is a jar of pickles older than the village.
Large Warehouse.why: Vanilla flavor: 'no room to swing a tail'.

Small Pile.content_md: Warehouses, piles and the underground pile
Small Pile.note: Large Pile and Underground Pile also keep all vanilla text.

Path.content_md: Paths, stairs, platforms, overhangs, bridges, gate, airlock and ziplines
Path.flavor: Every path in the village leads to a teahouse in the end.
Path.why: Vanilla flavor is a song about a lodge.

Stairs.flavor: The view from the top is worth the climb. The climb is still discussed afterwards.

Spiral Stairs.flavor: Cubs go up and down for fun. Adults go up once.
Spiral Stairs.why: Vanilla flavor is a quote from Suli, a beaver.

Platform.flavor: Bamboo scaffolding holds up most of the village and all of its laundry.
Platform.note: Double Platform keeps its vanilla flavor.

Triple Platform.flavor: Eating the scaffolding is strictly prohibited.
Triple Platform.why: Vanilla flavor: 'Gnawing on poles is strictly prohibited!' The Inkpaw version of the same sign.

Overhang.flavor: It sticks out over nothing and holds. Villagers test it with one paw first.
Overhang.why: Vanilla flavor is a quote from Pina, a beaver.
Overhang.note: One flavor key is shared by every overhang size (vanilla Building.Overhang.FlavorDescription).

Suspension Bridge.description: Allows villagers to pass over gaps.
Suspension Bridge.why: Vanilla description says 'Allows beavers to pass over gaps.'
Suspension Bridge.note: One description key is shared by every bridge size.

Metal Platform.flavor: Metal, for once. The village agreed it was necessary and still prefers bamboo.
Metal Platform.why: Vanilla flavor is a quote from Ma' Ngonel, a beaver.
Metal Platform.note: One flavor key is shared by both sizes (vanilla Building.MetalPlatform.FlavorDescription). Use only if the Inkpaws get metal platforms.

Airlock.description: Allows villagers to pass through while blocking off water.
Airlock.why: Vanilla description says 'Allows beavers to pass through'.

Zipline Station.content_md: Paths, stairs, platforms, overhangs, bridges, gate, airlock and ziplines
Zipline Station.flavor: The fastest a villager will ever travel. Most keep their eyes closed.
Zipline Station.why: Vanilla flavor: 'your tail must be this long'.

Zipline Pylon.flavor: Riders who pass each other wave politely and hold on tightly.
Zipline Pylon.why: Vanilla flavor mentions tails and beavers.

Zipline Beam.flavor: It holds the cable up. That is the whole job, and it does it well.
Zipline Beam.why: Vanilla flavor is a quote from Pina, a beaver.

Campfire.description: A place for villagers to relax and keep each other company.
Campfire.why: Vanilla says 'for beavers… in the evening'. Ringtails use it in the morning.

Hammock.name: Hammock
Hammock.description: A hammock for one. A nap here is part of every free afternoon.
Hammock.flavor: An Inkpaw can fall asleep in one faster than you can read this.
Hammock.note: The name equals the vanilla one, but the building satisfies the Nap need, so it needs its own description. The name may point at Building.Hammock.DisplayName.

Nap Platform.name: Nap Platform
Nap Platform.description: A deck where several villagers nap at once, on the ground or on a roof.
Nap Platform.flavor: There is room for several. Whoever arrives last naps on the stairs.

Teahouse.name: Teahouse
Teahouse.description: Serves roasted tea and water to villagers off duty. Closed while it has none.
Teahouse.flavor: Inkpaws fill it in the afternoon and Ringtails in the morning. The kettle never cools.

Slide and Swing.name: Slide and Swing
Slide and Swing.description: A playground with a slide and a swing, for villagers of all ages.
Slide and Swing.flavor: The slide is for the young. The queue is mostly adults.

Panda Kindergarten.name: Kindergarten
Panda Kindergarten.description: A quiet place to watch the young. It does adults a great deal of good.
Panda Kindergarten.flavor: Officially, the adults are here to supervise.

Ink Studio.name: Ink Studio
Ink Studio.description: A quiet room for ink painting and long thoughts.
Ink Studio.flavor: Most of the paintings are of bamboo. The rest are of bamboo in the rain.

Hot Spring Bath.name: Hot Spring Bath
Hot Spring Bath.description: A warm pool for a long soak. Uses water, and wets the fur.
Hot Spring Bath.flavor: Getting in takes a moment. Getting out takes resolve.

Opera Stage.name: Opera Stage
Opera Stage.description: Ringtail performers stage face-changing opera for whoever is off duty. Open while the performers work, from the afternoon bell to dawn.
Opera Stage.flavor: A new face with every turn of the head. The Ringtails will not say how it is done.

Teeth Grindstone.note: Vanilla text is true for pandas, who chew bamboo all day.

Medical Bed.description: Injured villagers lie here to rest and heal.
Medical Bed.flavor: The only bed in the village that anyone is in a hurry to leave.
Medical Bed.why: Vanilla says 'Injured beavers'; flavor is a quote from Pina, a beaver.

Herbalist.description: Creates antidote that cures contaminated villagers.

Night Builders' Post.name: Night Builders' Post
Night Builders' Post.description: Employs Ringtail builders who stock and raise construction sites from the afternoon bell to dawn.
Night Builders' Post.flavor: The Inkpaws go to bed beside a building site and wake up beside a building.

Night Courier Post.name: Night Courier Post
Night Courier Post.description: Employs Ringtail couriers who carry goods around the district from the afternoon bell to dawn. Ringtails run with their loads.
Night Courier Post.flavor: A full back-basket does not slow a Ringtail down. Neither does an empty one.

Night Forager's Post.name: Night Gatherers' Post
Night Forager's Post.description: Employs Ringtail gatherers who forage from the afternoon bell to dawn.
Night Forager's Post.flavor: Bamboo mushrooms are easiest to find by lantern light, or so the foragers insist.

Standing Lantern.name: Standing Lantern
Standing Lantern.description: A decorative lantern on a post.
Standing Lantern.flavor: Lit at the bell, one after another, by nobody in particular.

Hanging Lantern.name: Hanging Lantern
Hanging Lantern.description: A decorative lantern that hangs from a bracket.
Hanging Lantern.flavor: It swings a little whenever a Ringtail runs past.

String Lanterns.name: String Lanterns
String Lanterns.description: A string of small lanterns between two posts.
String Lanterns.flavor: Put up for one festival and never taken down.

Bamboo Fence.name: Bamboo Fence
Bamboo Fence.description: A decorative fence made from bamboo.
Bamboo Fence.flavor: It keeps nothing in and nothing out, and looks tidy doing it.

Hedge.note: The vanilla flavor (chewing through a hedge) is at least as true for pandas.

Potted Pine.name: Potted Pine
Potted Pine.description: A small pine tree trained in a pot.
Potted Pine.flavor: It has been the same size for longer than anyone can remember. That is the idea.

Panda Statue.name: Panda Statue
Panda Statue.description: A statue of a well-rested panda.

Bamboo Pinwheel.name: Bamboo Pinwheel
Bamboo Pinwheel.description: A small pinwheel that shows wind direction and strength.
Bamboo Pinwheel.flavor: Cubs blow on it to make the wind stronger. The kite windmills are not affected.

Pole Banner.flavor: Raised high so that everyone can see it and no cub or kit can reach it.
Pole Banner.why: Vanilla flavor blames 'kits' for vandalism. In this faction 'kits' means young Ringtails.

Goldfish Bowl.name: Goldfish Bowl
Goldfish Bowl.description: A decorative stone bowl with goldfish.
Goldfish Bowl.flavor: Somebody feeds them every day. Nobody knows who.

Garden Moon Gate.name: Garden Moon Gate
Garden Moon Gate.flavor: It leads from one side of the garden to the other side of the garden. Villagers walk through it anyway.

Roof.content_md: grey tile roofs in the vanilla sizes
Roof.note: All five sizes keep their vanilla names (Roof 1x1 … Roof 3x2) and the shared vanilla flavor.

Memorial Arch.name: Memorial Arch
Memorial Arch.description: A tall timber arch over the village road, raised for those who came before.
Memorial Arch.flavor: It carries no names. Everyone knows whom it is for.

Great Sitting Panda.name: Great Sitting Panda
Great Sitting Panda.description: A great cliff carving of a seated panda, with water running at its feet and a Ringtail on its shoulder.
Great Sitting Panda.flavor: It took generations to carve, and it has been sitting ever since.
Great Sitting Panda.note: Always 'cliff carving'. No religious words anywhere near this building.

Sky Lantern.name: Sky Lantern
Sky Lantern.description: A colossal sky lantern, launched with paper lanterns. Makes the villagers in the area extra happy.
Sky Lantern.flavor: It rises slowly, the way everything here does, and then it is gone over the hills.
Sky Lantern.note: The game adds the vanilla wonder keyword lines (Buildings.Wonder, Buildings.Wonder.Description) by itself. Buildings.Wonder says 'The pinnacle of beaver engineering'; see messages.json 'vanilla_lines_that_say_beaver'.

Automation.note: All vanilla text is kept. None of it mentions beavers. The Population Counter modes 'Total beavers' and 'Bots' are vanilla keys shared by every faction and are listed in messages.json 'vanilla_lines_that_say_beaver'.
